steps.text: Rules linking f and f′: f′ > 0 where f increases, f′ < 0 where f decreases, f′ = 0 at every turning point (local max/min) of f.
f decreases for x < 0, turns at x = 0 and increases for x > 0.
For a parabola f = ax² the derivative is the line 2ax through the origin with positive slope: graph B.
Rules linking f and f′: f′ > 0 where f increases, f′ < 0 where f decreases, f′ = 0 at every turning point (local max/min) of f.
f has minima at x ≈ ±1.4 and a maximum at x = 0, so f′ = 0 at these three x-values.
Signs: f′ < 0 far left, > 0 between −1.4 and 0, < 0 between 0 and 1.4, > 0 far right: a cubic starting low and ending high.

So f decreases then increases with a minimum at x = 0: a parabola opening up.

Rules linking f and f′: f′ > 0 where f increases, f′ < 0 where f decreases, f′ = 0 at every turning point (local max/min) of f.
f′ crosses zero three times: + then − then + then −.
So f increases, reaches a maximum, decreases to a minimum at 0, increases to a maximum, then decreases: two peaks with a dip between.

Rules linking f and f′: f′ > 0 where f increases, f′ < 0 where f decreases, f′ = 0 at every turning point (local max/min) of f.
f′ is a parabola with two zeros: + then − then +.
So f increases to a local maximum, decreases to a local minimum, then increases: a cubic shape.
